compressible.speed_of_sound.title: Speed of sound (a = sqrt(gamma R T))
assumptions: Ideal gas, constant gamma. For air at sea level (gamma = 1.4, R = 287 J/(kg K), T = 15 degC) this gives a ~ 340 m/s.

compressible.mach_angle.title: Mach angle (mu = asin(1/M))
assumptions: Only defined for M >= 1 (supersonic); mu is the half-angle of the Mach cone.

compressible.stagnation_ratios.title: Isentropic stagnation property ratios
assumptions: Isentropic (adiabatic, reversible) stagnation. Multiply by the static value to get the stagnation value: T0 = T (T0/T), etc.
method_references: Isentropic stagnation relations T0/T = 1 + (gamma-1)/2 M^2, P0/P = (...)^(gamma/(gamma-1))

compressible.isentropic_area_ratio.title: Isentropic area ratio A/A*
assumptions: A* is the throat (sonic) area. Two Mach numbers share one A/A* > 1; the subsonic root is returned when inverting unless the example favours the supersonic one (use area_ratio_inverse for both branches).

compressible.area_ratio_inverse.title: Inverse area-Mach: both Mach numbers for a given A/A*
assumptions: A/A* >= 1; A/A* = 1 gives M = 1. Solves by bisection on the isentropic area-Mach relation, so it is only as accurate as that ideal-gas model.
method_references: Inverse of the isentropic area-Mach relation (bisection)

compressible.choked_mass_flow.title: Choked (sonic throat) mass flow rate
assumptions: Choked flow at a sonic throat (M = 1). At the choked condition mdot is the maximum for the given stagnation state; gamma = 1.4 gives the constant (2/(gamma+1))^((gamma+1)/(2(gamma-1))) sqrt(gamma/R).
method_references: mdot = A* P0 / sqrt(T0) * sqrt(gamma/R) * (2/(gamma+1))^((gamma+1)/(2(gamma-1))) (recalled form)

compressible.normal_shock.title: Normal shock property ratios
assumptions: Stationary normal shock; the upstream is supersonic (M1 >= 1) and the downstream subsonic (M2 <= 1). Entropy rises across the shock, so the stagnation pressure ratio P02/P01 <= 1.

compressible.oblique_shock_theta.title: Oblique shock: deflection angle from M and shock angle (theta-beta-M)
assumptions: Supersonic upstream. A real shock needs M sin(beta) >= 1 (beta >= Mach angle); the relation then gives theta from 0 at the Mach angle back to 0 at a normal shock, with a maximum in between.
method_references: theta-beta-M relation, tan(theta) = 2 cot(beta) (M^2 sin^2(beta) - 1)/(M^2(gamma + cos 2beta) + 2)

compressible.oblique_shock.title: Oblique shock: weak and strong shock angles and downstream properties

procedure.python:
def _oblique_shock(values):
    """Oblique shock from (M, theta, gamma): weak and strong shock angles plus downstream properties."""
    M, theta, gamma = values['M'], values['theta'], values['gamma']
    beta_w, beta_s = _beta_weak_strong(M, theta, gamma)
    out = {}
    for tag, beta in (('weak', beta_w), ('strong', beta_s)):
        M1n = M * math.sin(beta)
        M2n, P2_P1, rho2_rho1, T2_T1 = _shock_ratios(M1n, gamma)
        out[f'beta_{tag}'] = beta
        out[f'M2_{tag}'] = M2n / math.sin(beta - theta)
        out[f'P2_P1_{tag}'] = P2_P1
        out[f'T2_T1_{tag}'] = T2_T1
        out[f'rho2_rho1_{tag}'] = rho2_rho1
    return out

assumptions: Attached oblique shock (theta below the detachment maximum; otherwise the shock is detached and this calculator raises). Weak solution is the one usually observed; the strong solution keeps M2 < 1. Downstream values use the normal shock on M1n = M sin(beta).
method_references: theta-beta-M weak/strong solution; normal-shock relations on the normal component

compressible.prandtl_meyer.title: Prandtl-Meyer expansion function
assumptions: nu(M) = 0 at M = 1 and rises to nu_max = pi/2 (sqrt((gamma+1)/(gamma-1)) - 1) as M -> inf. Across a centered expansion fan the turning is nu2 - nu1.

compressible.fanno_flow.title: Fanno flow (adiabatic constant-area duct with friction)
assumptions: Adiabatic, constant-area duct with constant Darcy friction factor f_D; * is the sonic (M = 1) reference state. The friction parameter f_D L*/D uses the Darcy factor (f_D = 4 f, with f the Fanning factor); the duct length needed to reach M = 1 from state M is L* = (f_D L*/D) D / f_D.

compressible.rayleigh_flow.title: Rayleigh flow (frictionless constant-area duct with heat addition)
assumptions: Frictionless, constant-area duct with heat addition; * is the sonic reference. Heat addition drives M toward 1 (thermal choking): subsonic flow speeds up, supersonic slows down.

compressible.nozzle_exit_velocity.title: Nozzle exit velocity (isentropic expansion from stagnation)
assumptions: Isentropic, adiabatic expansion from stagnation; P_e <= P0 (choked or unchoked as given). Equivalent to V_e = sqrt(2 gamma/(gamma-1) R T0 (1 - (P_e/P0)^((gamma-1)/gamma))).
method_references: Isentropic nozzle exit velocity from the steady-flow energy equation

compressible.nozzle_thrust.title: Rocket/nozzle thrust (momentum plus pressure term)
assumptions: Steady one-dimensional exit plane; the pressure term (P_e - P_a) A_e vanishes for a perfectly expanded nozzle (P_e = P_a).
method_references: F = mdot V_e + (P_e - P_a) A_e (steady momentum equation)
